87	+## Intent
88	+
89	+**Problem:** Once `VaultRepository.currentStatus` flips to `unlocked` (cold-start biometric/PIN success, spec-2-1/2-2), nothing ever re-locks it — an unlocked app stays unlocked indefinitely if backgrounded and left unattended, with no idle-based re-authentication trigger at all.
90	+
91	+**Approach:** Have `VaultRepositoryImpl` observe app-lifecycle transitions directly (`WidgetsBindingObserver`): record a timestamp on backgrounding, and on resume compare elapsed time against a new fixed domain constant; crossing it re-emits `VaultStatus.locked` through the existing `_emit`/`statusStream` machinery. The already-shipped AD-14 redirect (`VaultStatus` checked before `SessionStatus`) then bounces every screen back to `/vault` on that emission with zero router changes.
92	+
93	+## Boundaries & Constraints
94	+
95	+**Always:** Fixed `Duration(minutes: 5)` lives in a new `features/vault/domain` file, never a shared `core/` constant, never re-tuned by any later story. Elapsed time read via an injectable `DateTime Function() now` constructor param (default `DateTime.now`) for deterministic tests. Backgrounded timestamp recorded on `AppLifecycleState.paused`, read/cleared on `AppLifecycleState.resumed` — `inactive`/`hidden` are not treated as "backgrounded" on their own. Only emits `VaultStatus.locked` when `currentStatus` is currently `unlocked` AND elapsed `>= 5` minutes — never redundantly if already locked, never before the threshold. `WidgetsBinding.instance.addObserver(this)`/`removeObserver(this)` wired into the existing constructor/`dispose()` — no second observer, no new DI registration, no new `VaultStatus` enum value.
96	+
97	+**Ask First:** None.
98	+
99	+**Never:** No user-facing or account-level setting for this duration (fixed, not user-configurable — AC2). No `core/` constant. No new abstract method added to `VaultRepository`'s public contract. No changes to `app_router.dart` or `vault_lock_screen.dart` — the existing stream-driven redirect and `initState`-triggered `authenticate()` already cover re-prompting on relock.
100	+
101	+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
102	+
103	+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
104	+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
105	+| Backgrounded < 5 min, then resumed | `paused` at T0, was `unlocked`, `resumed` at T0+4min | `currentStatus` stays `unlocked`, no emission | N/A |
106	+| Backgrounded >= 5 min, then resumed | `paused` at T0, was `unlocked`, `resumed` at T0+5min (or later) | `statusStream` emits `locked`, `currentStatus` flips to `locked` | N/A |
107	+| Backgrounded >= 5 min while already locked | `paused` then `resumed` after >=5min, `currentStatus` already `locked` | stays `locked`, no duplicate emission | N/A |
108	+| `resumed` fires with no prior `paused` | e.g. first lifecycle callback ever observed | no-op, no emission, no crash | N/A |

+
+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** Once `VaultRepository.currentStatus` flips to `unlocked` (cold-start biometric/PIN success, spec-2-1/2-2), nothing ever re-locks it — an unlocked app stays unlocked indefinitely if backgrounded and left unattended, with no idle-based re-authentication trigger at all.
+
+**Approach:** Have `VaultRepositoryImpl` observe app-lifecycle transitions directly (`WidgetsBindingObserver`): record a timestamp on backgrounding, and on resume compare elapsed time against a new fixed domain constant; crossing it re-emits `VaultStatus.locked` through the existing `_emit`/`statusStream` machinery. The already-shipped AD-14 redirect (`VaultStatus` checked before `SessionStatus`) then bounces every screen back to `/vault` on that emission with zero router changes.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:** Fixed `Duration(minutes: 5)` lives in a new `features/vault/domain` file, never a shared `core/` constant, never re-tuned by any later story. Elapsed time read via an injectable `DateTime Function() now` constructor param (default `DateTime.now`) for deterministic tests. Backgrounded timestamp recorded on `AppLifecycleState.paused`, read/cleared on `AppLifecycleState.resumed` — `inactive`/`hidden` are not treated as "backgrounded" on their own. Only emits `VaultStatus.locked` when `currentStatus` is currently `unlocked` AND elapsed `>= 5` minutes — never redundantly if already locked, never before the threshold. `WidgetsBinding.instance.addObserver(this)`/`removeObserver(this)` wired into the existing constructor/`dispose()` — no second observer, no new DI registration, no new `VaultStatus` enum value.
+
+**Ask First:** None.
+
+**Never:** No user-facing or account-level setting for this duration (fixed, not user-configurable — AC2). No `core/` constant. No new abstract method added to `VaultRepository`'s public contract. No changes to `app_router.dart` or `vault_lock_screen.dart` — the existing stream-driven redirect and `initState`-triggered `authenticate()` already cover re-prompting on relock.
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| Backgrounded < 5 min, then resumed | `paused` at T0, was `unlocked`, `resumed` at T0+4min | `currentStatus` stays `unlocked`, no emission | N/A |
+| Backgrounded >= 5 min, then resumed | `paused` at T0, was `unlocked`, `resumed` at T0+5min (or later) | `statusStream` emits `locked`, `currentStatus` flips to `locked` | N/A |
+| Backgrounded >= 5 min while already locked | `paused` then `resumed` after >=5min, `currentStatus` already `locked` | stays `locked`, no duplicate emission | N/A |
+| `resumed` fires with no prior `paused` | e.g. first lifecycle callback ever observed | no-op, no emission, no crash | N/A |
+
+</frozen-after-approval>
+

+- [x] `lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart` -- implement `WidgetsBindingObserver`, injectable clock, add/removeObserver wiring, `didChangeAppLifecycleState` logic -- per I/O matrix.

No test covers two concurrent `submitPin` calls completing out of order.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

input.old_string:
- Given the app is backgrounded for 5 minutes or more, when I resume it, then re-authentication is always prompted regardless of any user setting, with the fixed 5-minute value living in `features/vault/domain`, never a shared `core/` constant.

## Spec Change Log
input.new_string:
- Given the app is backgrounded for 5 minutes or more, when I resume it, then re-authentication is always prompted regardless of any user setting, with the fixed 5-minute value living in `features/vault/domain`, never a shared `core/` constant.

### Review Findings

- [ ] [Review][Decision] Out-of-scope changes to `vault_lock_screen.dart` and `pin_keypad.dart` violate spec-2-3's explicit "Never" clause — this story's own frozen Boundaries say "No changes to `app_router.dart` or `vault_lock_screen.dart`," yet the diff attributed to this story (commit `81d7509`) modifies both `vault_lock_screen.dart` and the tightly-coupled `pin_keypad.dart` (the `submitPin` 10s timeout, the `PinKeypad.enabled` flag). Both are acknowledged leftover review fixes from story 2.2, bundled into this commit rather than committed separately. The idle-timeout logic itself fully complies with every other Boundary/Constraint and I/O-matrix row. Needs a human call: accept the bundling as-is (and amend the record), or split the commit/retroactively re-attribute the 2.2 fixes.
- [ ] [Review][Decision] A biometric/PIN unlock that resolves while the app is still backgrounded can trigger an immediate re-lock the moment the app resumes — `authenticate()` uses `persistAcrossBackgrounding: true` so a pending call can resolve after a `paused` is recorded; if `_emit(unlocked)` fires while still backgrounded and `resumed` arrives ≥5 minutes after the original `paused` (e.g. a long phone call), `didChangeAppLifecycleState` immediately re-locks, bouncing the user straight back to `/vault` right after they authenticated. Spec-2-3's I/O matrix doesn't define intended behavior for this interleaving — needs a product decision on whether a mid-background unlock should reset the idle clock. [lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:120-148]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `submitPin()`'s UI-level 10s timeout doesn't cancel the underlying repository call, so a second attempt can race the first against the same storage key — once the UI times out and re-enables the keypad, the original `VaultRepository.submitPin()` call keeps running; if it later resolves, it can emit `unlocked` from a stale, abandoned attempt, or race a concurrent first-time PIN write with no generation/cancellation token to make a stale result a no-op. [lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart:124] [lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:191]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] A second `paused` lifecycle event before any `resumed` silently resets the idle clock to the later timestamp — `didChangeAppLifecycleState` unconditionally overwrites `_backgroundedAt` on every `paused` with no check for an already-pending one, which can undercount true elapsed background time if `paused` ever fires twice without an intervening `resumed`. Not covered by the I/O matrix or tests. [lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:133]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `PinKeypad`'s `enabled: false` state has no visual or semantic disabled treatment — taps are silently swallowed in `_onDigitTap`/`_onBackspaceTap`, but `Semantics(button: true, ...)` never sets `enabled: false` and nothing dims the buttons, so neither a sighted nor a VoiceOver user gets any "processing"/disabled cue for up to 10 seconds. [lib/features/vault/presentation/widgets/pin_keypad.dart:233]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Stale error message lingers through a fresh PIN attempt with no "in progress" indicator — `_submitPin` never clears `_errorMessage` when a new attempt starts, so a previous mismatch/timeout message stays on screen unchanged through the new attempt. [lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart:124]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Test file registers two `VaultRepositoryImpl` instances as `WidgetsBindingObserver` on the same shared `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding` — the top-level `setUp()`'s `repository` and the idle-timeout group's own `idleRepository` both register on the same binding, so the "real dispatch path" test's `handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(...)` notifies both simultaneously with no assertion covering the unintended side effect. Currently harmless (verified: full suite passes, `repository` never reaches `unlocked` in that group), but an unnecessary double registration. [test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Constructor's `WidgetsBinding.instance.addObserver(this)` depends entirely on binding-init ordering, backed only by a comment — every current call site is correctly ordered (no live bug today), but there's no runtime assertion, so any future direct construction outside that ordering would crash with an opaque Flutter-binding error instead of a clear, intentional one. [lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:48]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] spec-2-3's own review-tracking metadata is incomplete and internally inconsistent — frontmatter `review_loop_iteration: 0` remains at its initial value even though this file's own "Suggested Review Order" section repeatedly says "Added in review," and unlike spec-2-1/spec-2-2 in this same diff, spec-2-3 has no populated `### Review Findings` section at all until this edit. [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-2-3-fixed-5-minute-idle-re-authentication-timeout.md]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] spec-2-3 frontmatter status disagrees with `sprint-status.yaml` — this file's frontmatter sets `status: 'done'` while the same diff's `sprint-status.yaml` sets `2-3-fixed-5-minute-idle-re-authentication-timeout: review`. [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-2-3-fixed-5-minute-idle-re-authentication-timeout.md:5] [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml:198]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `test-summary.md` has no "Story 2.3" section despite this diff shipping the full implementation and 7 new tests — unlike the full "Story 2.2"/"QA Generate E2E Tests Pass" sections in the same file, there is no "Story 2.3" section, and its own "Next Steps" text calling 2.3 still-upcoming is left stale by the very same diff that ships 2.3's code and tests. [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `deferred-work.md`'s new clock-skew entry gives a justification that doesn't actually distinguish its two options — it argues wall-clock `DateTime.now()` is kept partly because a monotonic `Stopwatch` "doesn't survive the app process being killed while backgrounded," but the current plain `DateTime?` field is lost identically on process death. The actual reasons to prefer `DateTime` (simplicity, no new dependency) are sound; only this one stated justification is inconsistent. [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md]

## Intent

**Problem:** Once `VaultRepository.currentStatus` flips to `unlocked` (cold-start biometric/PIN success, spec-2-1/2-2), nothing ever re-locks it — an unlocked app stays unlocked indefinitely if backgrounded and left unattended, with no idle-based re-authentication trigger at all.

**Approach:** Have `VaultRepositoryImpl` observe app-lifecycle transitions directly (`WidgetsBindingObserver`): record a timestamp on backgrounding, and on resume compare elapsed time against a new fixed domain constant; crossing it re-emits `VaultStatus.locked` through the existing `_emit`/`statusStream` machinery. The already-shipped AD-14 redirect (`VaultStatus` checked before `SessionStatus`) then bounces every screen back to `/vault` on that emission with zero router changes.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** Fixed `Duration(minutes: 5)` lives in a new `features/vault/domain` file, never a shared `core/` constant, never re-tuned by any later story. Elapsed time read via an injectable `DateTime Function() now` constructor param (default `DateTime.now`) for deterministic tests. Backgrounded timestamp recorded on `AppLifecycleState.paused`, read/cleared on `AppLifecycleState.resumed` — `inactive`/`hidden` are not treated as "backgrounded" on their own. Only emits `VaultStatus.locked` when `currentStatus` is currently `unlocked` AND elapsed `>= 5` minutes — never redundantly if already locked, never before the threshold. `WidgetsBinding.instance.addObserver(this)`/`removeObserver(this)` wired into the existing constructor/`dispose()` — no second observer, no new DI registration, no new `VaultStatus` enum value.

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No user-facing or account-level setting for this duration (fixed, not user-configurable — AC2). No `core/` constant. No new abstract method added to `VaultRepository`'s public contract. No changes to `app_router.dart` or `vault_lock_screen.dart` — the existing stream-driven redirect and `initState`-triggered `authenticate()` already cover re-prompting on relock.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Backgrounded < 5 min, then resumed | `paused` at T0, was `unlocked`, `resumed` at T0+4min | `currentStatus` stays `unlocked`, no emission | N/A |
| Backgrounded >= 5 min, then resumed | `paused` at T0, was `unlocked`, `resumed` at T0+5min (or later) | `statusStream` emits `locked`, `currentStatus` flips to `locked` | N/A |
| Backgrounded >= 5 min while already locked | `paused` then `resumed` after >=5min, `currentStatus` already `locked` | stays `locked`, no duplicate emission | N/A |
| `resumed` fires with no prior `paused` | e.g. first lifecycle callback ever observed | no-op, no emission, no crash | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

No `clock`/`fake_async` package is pinned in `pubspec.yaml` and none is being added for this — testability is achieved with a plain injectable `DateTime Function() now` parameter (default `DateTime.now`), the simplest decide-and-proceed fit given no existing clock-injection pattern elsewhere in the codebase. `paused`/`resumed` are the chosen pair because they bound iOS's actual background/foreground transition (`resumed → inactive → hidden → paused` and its reverse) — treating `inactive`/`hidden` alone as "backgrounded" would false-trigger on transient interruptions like Control Center or an incoming call.

# Story 2.3 — Fixed 5-Minute Idle Re-Authentication Timeout

## Context

Story 2.3 adds idle-based re-authentication: `VaultRepositoryImpl` observes
app-lifecycle transitions directly (`WidgetsBindingObserver`), records a
timestamp on `AppLifecycleState.paused`, and on `resumed` re-emits
`VaultStatus.locked` if `vaultIdleTimeout` (a fixed 5-minute,
domain-owned constant) has elapsed while the vault was `unlocked`. The
code-review pass on this diff fixed four issues found in that logic and
its neighbors — see "Generated Tests" below for what was added for each.

## Generated Tests

### Unit (`VaultRepositoryImpl`)

- [x] `test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart`
  — **new** `didChangeAppLifecycleState() — idle re-authentication
  (spec-2-3)` group: all four frozen I/O-matrix rows (backgrounded < 5min
  stays unlocked, >= 5min re-locks, already-locked has no duplicate
  emission, bare `resumed` with no prior `paused` no-ops) via an
  injectable fake clock; a real `WidgetsBinding`-dispatched case proving
  the constructor's `addObserver(this)` wiring is actually in effect;
  `inactive`/`hidden` confirmed as no-ops; a tight boundary case one
  second short of the threshold.
  — **added by the code-review pass**: a case proving a mid-background
  unlock (e.g. a persisted biometric call resolving while still `paused`)
  resets the idle clock rather than immediately re-locking on the next
  `resume`; a case proving a second `paused` before any `resumed` keeps
  the earliest timestamp instead of resetting it; a case proving a
  superseded (stale) `submitPin` call — one whose UI-level timeout already
  fired and was retried — never mutates storage or emits `unlocked`.

## Coverage

- Idle re-lock I/O matrix (all four frozen rows) ✅, real-dispatch wiring
  proof ✅, `inactive`/`hidden` no-op ✅, tight threshold boundary ✅ (all
  from the story's own implementation pass)
- Mid-background unlock resets the idle clock ✅, double-`paused` keeps
  the earliest timestamp ✅, superseded `submitPin` call is a safe no-op
  ✅ (all added by the code-review pass)
- Implemented feature scope (per `sprint-status.yaml`): stories 1.1–1.6,
  2.1, 2.2, and 2.3 — all covered.

## Verification

- `fvm flutter test` → all passing (pre-existing suite + this pass's new
  idle-timeout and code-review cases)
- `fvm flutter analyze` → 0 issues

## Next Steps

- Story 2.4 (biometric preference persistence) is the next `backlog`
  story in Epic 2.

# Story 2.3 — Fixed 5-Minute Idle Re-Authentication Timeout

## Context

Story 2.3 adds idle-based re-authentication: `VaultRepositoryImpl` observes
app-lifecycle transitions directly (`WidgetsBindingObserver`), records a
timestamp on `AppLifecycleState.paused`, and on `resumed` re-emits
`VaultStatus.locked` if `vaultIdleTimeout` (a fixed 5-minute,
domain-owned constant) has elapsed while the vault was `unlocked`. The
code-review pass on this diff fixed four issues found in that logic and
its neighbors — see "Generated Tests" below for what was added for each.

## Generated Tests

### Unit (`VaultRepositoryImpl`)

- [x] `test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart`
  — **new** `didChangeAppLifecycleState() — idle re-authentication
  (spec-2-3)` group: all four frozen I/O-matrix rows (backgrounded < 5min
  stays unlocked, >= 5min re-locks, already-locked has no duplicate
  emission, bare `resumed` with no prior `paused` no-ops) via an
  injectable fake clock; a real `WidgetsBinding`-dispatched case proving
  the constructor's `addObserver(this)` wiring is actually in effect;
  `inactive`/`hidden` confirmed as no-ops; a tight boundary case one
  second short of the threshold.
  — **added by the code-review pass**: a case proving a mid-background
  unlock (e.g. a persisted biometric call resolving while still `paused`)
  resets the idle clock rather than immediately re-locking on the next
  `resume`; a case proving a second `paused` before any `resumed` keeps
  the earliest timestamp instead of resetting it; a case proving a
  superseded (stale) `submitPin` call — one whose UI-level timeout already
  fired and was retried — never mutates storage or emits `unlocked`.

## Coverage

- Idle re-lock I/O matrix (all four frozen rows) ✅, real-dispatch wiring
  proof ✅, `inactive`/`hidden` no-op ✅, tight threshold boundary ✅ (all
  from the story's own implementation pass)
- Mid-background unlock resets the idle clock ✅, double-`paused` keeps
  the earliest timestamp ✅, superseded `submitPin` call is a safe no-op
  ✅ (all added by the code-review pass)
- Implemented feature scope (per `sprint-status.yaml`): stories 1.1–1.6,
  2.1, 2.2, and 2.3 — all covered.

## Verification

56	
57	- [x] [Review][Decision] Out-of-scope changes to `vault_lock_screen.dart` and `pin_keypad.dart` violate spec-2-3's explicit "Never" clause — this story's own frozen Boundaries say "No changes to `app_router.dart` or `vault_lock_screen.dart`," yet the diff attributed to this story (commit `81d7509`) modifies both `vault_lock_screen.dart` and the tightly-coupled `pin_keypad.dart` (the `submitPin` 10s timeout, the `PinKeypad.enabled` flag). Both are acknowledged leftover review fixes from story 2.2, bundled into this commit rather than committed separately. The idle-timeout logic itself fully complies with every other Boundary/Constraint and I/O-matrix row. — resolved: accepted as documented (see Spec Change Log below). The bundled fixes are real, correct, and already explained in `test-summary.md`/`deferred-work.md`; no code or history change made.
58	- [ ] [Review][Patch] A biometric/PIN unlock that resolves while the app is still backgrounded can trigger an immediate re-lock the moment the app resumes — `authenticate()` uses `persistAcrossBackgrounding: true` so a pending call can resolve after a `paused` is recorded; if `_emit(unlocked)` fires while still backgrounded and `resumed` arrives ≥5 minutes after the original `paused` (e.g. a long phone call), `didChangeAppLifecycleState` immediately re-locks, bouncing the user straight back to `/vault` right after they authenticated. — resolution: clear `_backgroundedAt` whenever `_emit(unlocked)` fires, so any unlock always resets the idle clock regardless of the app's current lifecycle state. [lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:108-117]
59	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `submitPin()`'s UI-level 10s timeout doesn't cancel the underlying repository call, so a second attempt can race the first against the same storage key — once the UI times out and re-enables the keypad, the original `VaultRepository.submitPin()` call keeps running; if it later resolves, it can emit `unlocked` from a stale, abandoned attempt, or race a concurrent first-time PIN write with no generation/cancellation token to make a stale result a no-op. Not covered by the I/O matrix or tests. [lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:133]
61	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `PinKeypad`'s `enabled: false` state has no visual or semantic disabled treatment — taps are silently swallowed in `_onDigitTap`/`_onBackspaceTap`, but `Semantics(button: true, ...)` never sets `enabled: false` and nothing dims the buttons, so neither a sighted nor a VoiceOver user gets any "processing"/disabled cue for up to 10 seconds. [lib/features/vault/presentation/widgets/pin_keypad.dart:233]
62	- [ ] [Review][Patch] Stale error message lingers through a fresh PIN attempt with no "in progress" indicator — `_submitPin` never clears `_errorMessage` when a new attempt starts, so a previous mismatch/timeout message stays on screen unchanged through the new attempt. [lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart:124]
63	- [ ] [Review][Patch] Test file registers two `VaultRepositoryImpl` instances as `WidgetsBindingObserver` on the same shared `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding` — the top-level `setUp()`'s `repository` and the idle-timeout group's own `idleRepository` both register on the same binding, so the "real dispatch path" test's `handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(...)` notifies both simultaneously with no assertion covering the unintended side effect. Currently harmless (verified: full suite passes, `repository` never reaches `unlocked` in that group), but an unnecessary double registration. [test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart]

[lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:48]

[_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-2-3-fixed-5-minute-idle-re-authentication-timeout.md:5] [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml:198]

[_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md]
